learnings.title: GitHub: self-serve confirmed hands-on, plus an undocumented callback parameter
learnings.detail: A tester registered an OAuth App and completed authorization in a few minutes with no review, as the guide says. The callback also carried iss=https://github.com/login/oauth (RFC 9207), which GitHub's OAuth docs don't mention. We added it as a Tested nuance.

learnings.title: Slack's 'Create new app' dialog changed; our checklist was out of date
learnings.detail: The dialog now offers AI agent, Starter app, From a manifest and Blank app. 'From scratch' is gone. The curated Slack guide already said 'Blank app' because it was built from current docs, but our manual checklist said 'From scratch' and confused the tester. Creating a new workspace also pushed paid-plan upsells, which a developer can skip by staying on the Free plan or using a Developer Program sandbox.

learnings.title: Slack: install worked hands-on; the settings form accepted an http:// redirect URL
learnings.detail: The OAuth v2 install into the tester's own workspace worked with no review, as the guide says. But the OAuth & Permissions page saved http://example.com/x even though Slack's docs and our guide said HTTPS is required. We corrected the guide to separate what the docs say from what the form enforces, and left the authorize-time behaviour as an open question.

learnings.title: Google: Gmail scopes are hidden until the Gmail API is enabled
learnings.detail: The tester couldn't find any gmail scopes under Data Access. The console only lists scopes for enabled APIs ('Only scopes for enabled APIs are listed below'). The curated guide already has 'Enable the Gmail, Calendar and Drive APIs' as its own step, but our shorter manual checklist skipped it, so the checklist was fixed. Lesson: order matters, and a skipped prerequisite step looks like a missing feature.
